issues.description: The problem specification and provided Main use a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon to receive ingredient deliveries, but the solution implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This name/signature mismatch (method expected by the spec/Main vs. method provided by the solution) will confuse students and break code that calls acceptSupplyDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name and signature consistent with the problem statement and template Main. Rename the solution's receiveDelivery method to acceptSupplyDelivery with the same parameters (String name, int price, int quantity), or add a static wrapper acceptSupplyDelivery that delegates to receiveDelivery. Ensure the method is static as specified.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize SealSaloon attributes (orders and stock) in the constructor, but elsewhere the statement requires the stock attribute to be static and final (shared across instances). Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is contradictory and would either be illegal (final reassignment) or confusing. This is an internal specification contradiction about where/how the static final stock should be initialized.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify initialization guidance: if stock must be static final (shared across instances), instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer rather than in the constructor. Alternatively, remove the requirement that stock be static/final and require per-instance initialization in the constructor. Make the intended approach explicit.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a static method named 'acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int)' to receive stock deliveries, and the template's Main invokes shop.acceptSupplyDelivery(...). The solution implementation instead provides a static method named 'receiveDelivery(String, int, int)'. This inconsistent method name for the same conceptual operation creates confusion for students mapping the requirement to the implementation and breaks direct correspondence with the template example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's receiveDelivery method to acceptSupplyDelivery with the same signature (public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)), and update any internal references accordingly so the solution, template, and problem statement use the same method name.
